On pp. 15-16, private ramification at t_b proves disjointness for fixed v. It does not make the diagonal inertia vector generate the product when v varies. For a nonsplit GL_2 representation over F_p, H(1) and (H+E)(1) generate the same upper-triangular adjoint submodule with quotient Q = F_p(kappa); both basis vectors have equal nonzero image in Q. The difference of their variable theta classes is unramified at v and belongs to the finite H1 with fixed ramification set. Two distinct v therefore give a nonzero linear relation on the four projected Galois groups. Lemma 3.7 as universally stated is false. The consequent independence assertions in Proposition 3.8 and Theorem 4.4 need a new proof; no repair of the main theorems is established by this verification.

The p. 18 argument again applies generation of an individual image to a product: all h classes ramify at t_0, so cancellation there is possible. For nonsplit rho with chi = kappa, the root line E and the quotient of the cyclic module generated by H(1) are both Q = F_p(kappa). On an infinite subfamily fix the nonzero inertia scalar of h at a and subtract a scalar multiple of the quotient of eta_b^(a). This Q-valued class is unramified at a and lies in a finite H1 with ramification in T. Two choices a != a' coincide, yielding h^(a)-h^(a') = lambda f(eta_b^(a)-eta_b^(a')) on Gamma_K, nonzero at a. Thus the two composites have a nontrivial common quotient field. The claimed arbitrary-composite disjointness and its use on pp. 19 and 22 are not justified.

The SO_2n maximal-isotropic Levi acts on u by exterior-square standard, as p. 48 states. An invariant in exterior-square rho_M tensor kappa is an alternating bivector with eigencharacter kappa^(-1). Under absolute irreducibility it is nondegenerate; its inverse is an alternating form with multiplier kappa^(-1), rather than kappa. Item 82 copies the wrong sign in A.11(4)(b). Record a separate source correction and retain the nondegeneracy argument.

The p. 55 presentation and item 94 omit relations from fixing the torus character on inertia. For a nonzero crystalline extension r of 1 by epsilon over Q_p, the cup-product connecting map from H1(t) to H2(E(1)) is onto, so H2(r(b)) = 0. The image on inertial torus cohomology has dimension 1, giving B-lift tangent dimension 5 and flagged tangent dimension 6. Page 54 identifies this completion as a quotient of the potentially semistable ring of dimension 5. It cannot be a six-variable power-series ring with zero relations. Counting at most H2(r(b)) + [K:Q_p] dim(t) relations before minimizing the presentation gives the needed lower bound; use distinct new source-issue ids for findings 19 and 20, including the fixed-multiplier case.
